text:
Abstract
The objective was to determine how many sequencing runs in the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) are annotated for Escherichia coli. Because organism queries to ENA operate via NCBI Taxonomy identifiers, we first resolved the organism name to its NCBI taxon. An initial lookup for the misspelled “Escherichia colli” returned zero records. We then corrected the organism to “Escherichia coli,” which resolved to taxon ID 562. Using the BRC Analytics ENA proxy to list runs by taxonomy ID, we queried ENA for taxid 562 and read its reported total count field. The ENA total run count for Escherichia coli (taxid 562) was 551,679 at the time of query, with one representative run returned in the page to confirm the query context (page size 1, offset 0). This count measures sequencing effort and can be used to scope downstream analyses, such as subsetting by library strategy or study and estimating data-processing resources. All results trace to the exact API calls listed under References.

I. Introduction
Background. Escherichia coli is a widely studied bacterial species, and ENA holds raw sequencing runs across many studies and strategies. Knowing the run count is useful for planning data retrieval and analysis at scale.
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.
Knowledge Gap. The exact, current ENA run count for E. coli was not specified.
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: resolve the organism to its NCBI taxon and retrieve the ENA run total for Escherichia coli. Hypothesis: correcting the organism spelling to “Escherichia coli” will yield a large run count.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We used NCBI Taxonomy to resolve the organism name to a taxon ID, then queried ENA (via BRC Analytics’ proxy) for the total number of runs annotated with that taxon.
Materials.
- NCBI Taxonomy (functions.ncbi_taxonomy_lookup)
- ENA via BRC Analytics proxy (functions.brc_ena_runs)
Procedures.
- ncbi_taxonomy_lookup with query="Escherichia colli".
- ncbi_taxonomy_lookup with query="Escherichia coli".
- brc_ena_runs with taxonomy_id="562", limit=1, offset=0 to obtain total_in_ena and confirm a representative run.
Statistical Analysis.
- NCBI Taxonomy: result_count was read from the tool’s provenance for each query (0 for the misspelling, 1 for the corrected name).
- ENA runs: total_in_ena was read directly from the brc_ena_runs response; returned and offset confirm page parameters. No deduplication was performed; the count is as reported by ENA for taxid 562.

III. Results
Data Presentation.
Table 1. Resolution and ENA counts for Escherichia coli.

| Metric                                              | Value    |
|-----------------------------------------------------|----------|
| NCBI Taxonomy matches for “Escherichia colli”       | 0        |
| NCBI Taxonomy matches for “Escherichia coli”        | 1        |
| NCBI Taxonomy ID for Escherichia coli               | 562      |
| ENA total runs for taxid 562 (total_in_ena)         | 551679   |
| Page returned (brc_ena_runs ‘returned’)             | 1        |
| Offset (brc_ena_runs ‘offset’)                      | 0        |
Findings.
- ENA holds 551,679 runs for Escherichia coli (taxid 562).

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The ENA total run count for Escherichia coli is 551,679. The objective was met after correcting the organism spelling and using the species taxon ID 562.
Context. The initial misspelling (“colli”) produced no taxonomy record; the corrected query resolved to 562 and yielded the ENA total.
Limitations. The count reflects runs annotated with taxid 562. Runs annotated under strain-specific taxids distinct from 562 may not be included. ENA is continuously updated; counts can change over time. The query used a single-page fetch with limit=1 only to confirm context; the total_in_ena field is the reported aggregate and no independent recrawl was performed.
Conclusion & Future Directions. ENA currently lists 551,679 Escherichia coli runs (taxid 562). Future queries could stratify by library strategy (e.g., WGS vs. RNA-Seq), study accession, instrument model, or track first-public dates to assess temporal trends.

References
[1] NCBI Taxonomy — esearch for “Escherichia colli”: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi?term=Escherichia+colli&retmax=50&retstart=0&sort=relevance&retmode=json&db=taxonomy&tool=fdea-ncbi-mcp&email=jonathangunti%40gmail.com
[2] NCBI Taxonomy — esearch/efetch for “Escherichia coli” (taxid 562): https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi?term=Escherichia+coli&retmax=50&retstart=0&sort=relevance&retmode=json&db=taxonomy&tool=fdea-ncbi-mcp&email=jonathangunti%40gmail.com; https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?id=562&retmode=xml&db=taxonomy&tool=fdea-ncbi-mcp&email=jonathangunti%40gmail.com
[3] ENA via BRC Analytics — runs for taxid 562 (total_in_ena=551679): https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/ena/taxonomy/562

Acknowledgments
We thank NCBI Taxonomy and the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA), accessed via BRC Analytics’ proxy, for the data used in this analysis.
